lesson_scope: Equilibrium of particles suspended by strings from two fixed supports; geometric determination of string angles; simultaneous equations for string tensions; symmetrical and asymmetrical two-string systems; perpendicular force triangle methods; continuous strings over smooth pegs and smooth rings; and analysis of string tension limits and breaking thresholds.

questions.difficulty_reason: Foundational Drill: Drill 1: Symmetrical two-string suspension under gravity

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Drill 1: Symmetrical two-string suspension under gravity

hints: Because the two strings have identical lengths and symmetric attachment points, their tensions must be equal: $T_1 = T_2 = T$.
Resolve vertically: the combined vertical components of both strings support the weight: $2 T\sin 30^\circ = 60 \implies 2 T(0.5) = 60 \implies T = 60\text{ N}$.

walkthrough.text:
Equate the tensions using horizontal symmetry:
$$\Sigma F_x = T_2\cos 30^\circ - T_1\cos 30^\circ = 0 \implies T_1 = T_2 = T$$

Resolve vertically in equilibrium to find $T$:
$$\Sigma F_y = 2 T\sin 30^\circ - 60 = 0$$
$$2 T(0.5) = 60 \implies T = 60\text{ N}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Recognize the geometric symmetry:
- Both strings pull at the same angle of $30^\circ$ on opposite sides.
- Horizontal cancellation requires equal tensions:
$$T_1 = T_2 = T$$

Balance the vertical load:
- Each string provides an upward pull of $T\sin 30^\circ = 0.5 T$.
- Together, they carry the entire $60\text{ N}$ weight:
$$2(0.5 T) = 60 \implies T = 60\text{ N}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Applies symmetry to deduce equal tensions and sets up vertical equilibrium: $2 T\sin 30^\circ = 60$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Foundational Drill: Drill 2: Symmetrical suspension with vertical angles

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Drill 2: Symmetrical suspension with vertical angles

hints: Notice that the angle is given with the vertical, so the upward vertical component of each string is $T\cos 45^\circ$.
Set $2 T\cos 45^\circ = mg = 2(10) = 20\text{ N}$, giving $T\sqrt{2} = 20 \implies T = 10\sqrt{2} \approx 14.1\text{ N}$.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate the weight of the package:
$$W = mg = 2(10) = 20\text{ N}$$

Resolve forces vertically in equilibrium to find tension $T$:
$$\Sigma F_y = 2 T\cos 45^\circ - 20 = 0$$
$$2 T\left(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right) = 20 \implies T\sqrt{2} = 20$$
$$T = \frac{20}{\sqrt{2}} = 10\sqrt{2} \approx 14.142 \approx 14.1\text{ N}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Find the downward gravitational pull:
- Package mass is $2\text{ kg}$, giving weight:
$$W = mg = 2 \times 10 = 20\text{ N}$$
Because both strings make $45^\circ$ with the vertical, the two tensions are equal by symmetry.

Resolve vertically:
- Each string provides upward support $T\cos 45^\circ$:
$$2 T\cos 45^\circ = 20 \implies T\sqrt{2} = 20 \implies T = 10\sqrt{2} \approx 14.1\text{ N}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Calculates weight $W = 2(10) = 20\text{ N}$ and sets up vertical equilibrium: $2 T\cos 45^\circ = 20$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Foundational Drill: Drill 3: Particle held by one horizontal string and one angled string

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Drill 3: Particle held by one horizontal string and one angled string

hints: Notice that String 1 is horizontal and has zero vertical component, so String 2 must support the entire vertical weight alone.

Resolve vertically: $T_2\sin 60^\circ = 30\sqrt{3} \implies T_2\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = 30\sqrt{3} \implies T_2 = 60\text{ N}$. Then resolve horizontally: $T_1 = T_2\cos 60^\circ = 60(0.5) = 30\text{ N}$.

walkthrough.text:
Resolve forces vertically in equilibrium to isolate $T_2$:
$$\Sigma F_y = T_2\sin 60^\circ - 30\sqrt{3} = 0$$
$$T_2\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = 30\sqrt{3} \implies T_2 = \frac{60\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{3}} = 60\text{ N}$$

Resolve forces horizontally in equilibrium to find $T_1$:
$$\Sigma F_x = T_2\cos 60^\circ - T_1 = 0$$
$$T_1 = T_2\cos 60^\circ = 60(0.5) = 30\text{ N}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Isolate the vertical axis first:
- String 1 is horizontal, contributing zero upward support.
- String 2 must bear the full downward load of $30\sqrt{3}\text{ N}$:
$$T_2\sin 60^\circ = 30\sqrt{3}\text{ N} \implies T_2 = 60\text{ N}$$

Balance the horizontal forces:
- String 1 pulls horizontally to counter the horizontal component of string 2:
$$T_1 = T_2\cos 60^\circ = 60 \times 0.5 = 30\text{ N}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Solves to obtain $T_2 = 60\text{ N}$ and resolves horizontally to obtain $T_1 = T_2\cos 60^\circ = 30\text{ N}$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Foundational Drill: Drill 4: Perpendicular string geometry from suspension lengths

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Drill 4: Perpendicular string geometry from suspension lengths

hints: Check the Pythagorean triple $5-12-13$: $0.5^2 + 1.2^2 = 0.25 + 1.44 = 1.69 = 1.3^2$, so the angle at $P$ is $90^\circ$.

Because string $BP$ is perpendicular to $AP$, resolving along $AP$ eliminates $T_B$. The angle between string $AP$ and the downward vertical is the complement of $\angle PAB$, giving $T_A = 26\left(\frac{1.2}{1.3}\right) = 24\text{ N}$.

walkthrough.text:
Verify the perpendicularity of the strings:
$$AP^2 + BP^2 = 0.5^2 + 1.2^2 = 0.25 + 1.44 = 1.69 = 1.3^2 = AB^2$$
Thus, $\angle APB = 90^\circ$.

Resolve along string $AP$ (perpendicular to string $BP$):
$$\cos\phi = \frac{BP}{AB} = \frac{1.2}{1.3} = \frac{12}{13}$$
$$T_A = W\cos\phi = 26\left(\frac{12}{13}\right) = 2 \times 12 = 24\text{ N}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Notice the scaled $5-12-13$ triangle:
- $0.5^2 + 1.2^2 = 1.3^2$, so $\angle APB = 90^\circ$.
- The two string tensions are perpendicular:
$$\angle APB = 90^\circ$$

Resolve along string $AP$:
- String $BP$ has zero component along $AP$.
- The component of weight along $AP$ gives tension directly:
$$T_A = 26 \times \frac{1.2}{1.3} = 24\text{ N}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Confirms $0.5^2 + 1.2^2 = 1.3^2$ and identifies $\cos\theta_A = \sin\angle PAB = \frac{1.2}{1.3} = \frac{12}{13}$ with the vertical.
Resolves along string $AP$ to obtain $T_A = 26\left(\frac{12}{13}\right) = 24\text{ N}$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Foundational Drill: Drill 5: Maximum suspended mass under string tension threshold

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Drill 5: Maximum suspended mass under string tension threshold

hints: At the breaking limit, the tension in both strings reaches $T = 150\text{ N}$.
Resolve vertically: $2 T\sin 20^\circ = Mg$. Substitute $T = 150\text{ N}$ and $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$ to find $M = \frac{300\sin 20^\circ}{10} = 30\sin 20^\circ \approx 10.3\text{ kg}$.

walkthrough.text:
Set up the vertical equilibrium equation at maximum allowable tension $T = 150\text{ N}$:
$$\Sigma F_y = 2 T\sin 20^\circ - Mg = 0$$
$$2(150)\sin 20^\circ = 10 M \implies 300\sin 20^\circ = 10 M$$

Solve for the maximum mass $M$:
$$M = 30\sin 20^\circ \approx 30(0.34202) = 10.2606 \approx 10.3\text{ kg}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Identify the breaking condition:
- Each string can pull with at most $150\text{ N}$.
- Symmetrical suspension means both strings reach this limit at the same time:
$$T_1 = T_2 = 150\text{ N}$$

Calculate the supported weight and mass:
- Combined upward support:
$$2(150\sin 20^\circ) = 300(0.3420) \approx 102.6\text{ N}$$
- Dividing by $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$ gives the maximum safe mass:
$$M = \frac{102.6}{10} \approx 10.3\text{ kg}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Sets up limiting vertical equilibrium: $2(150)\sin 20^\circ = 10 M$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Drill 6: Single continuous string across two smooth pegs

hints: Because the pegs are smooth, the tension $T$ is uniform throughout the string and equals the weight of each hanging mass: $T = 4(10) = 40\text{ N}$.
At the central block, both upward string segments contribute $T\sin 30^\circ$. Set $2 T\sin 30^\circ = Mg \implies 2(40)(0.5) = 10 M \implies 40 = 10 M \implies M = 4\text{ kg}$.

walkthrough.text:
Determine the uniform tension from the hanging masses:
Because the pegs are smooth, tension is constant throughout the string:
$$T = m_\text{end} g = 4(10) = 40\text{ N}$$

Resolve forces vertically at the central mass $M$:
$$\Sigma F_y = 2 T\sin 30^\circ - Mg = 0$$
$$2(40)(0.5) = 10 M \implies 40 = 10 M \implies M = 4\text{ kg}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Find the uniform tension:
- The hanging masses of $4\text{ kg}$ set the tension throughout the continuous string:
$$T = 4 \times 10 = 40\text{ N}$$

Balance the central block:
- Both slanted segments pull upwards with $T\sin 30^\circ = 40 \times 0.5 = 20\text{ N}$.
- Total upward lift is $20 + 20 = 40\text{ N}$, which balances $Mg$:
$$10 M = 40 \implies M = 4\text{ kg}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Identifies uniform tension $T = 4g = 40\text{ N}$ and sets up vertical equilibrium at the central block: $2 T\sin 30^\circ = Mg$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured Practice: Core Practice 1: Two-string ceiling suspension with complementary inclinations

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Core Practice 1: Two-string ceiling suspension with complementary inclinations

hints: Consider the horizontal line through $O$: string $OA$ is at $40^\circ$ above the horizontal to the left, and $OB$ is at $50^\circ$ above the horizontal to the right. The angle between them is $180^\circ - (40^\circ + 50^\circ) = 90^\circ$.
Resolve horizontally: the leftward component $T_A\cos 40^\circ$ balances the rightward component $T_B\cos 50^\circ$, giving $T_B = T_A\frac{\cos 40^\circ}{\cos 50^\circ} = T_A\tan 50^\circ$.

walkthrough.text:
Verify the angle between the strings:
Taking the horizontal line passing through point $O$:
$$\angle AOB = 180^\circ - 40^\circ - 50^\circ = 90^\circ$$
Therefore, the strings $OA$ and $OB$ are perpendicular to each other.

Resolve forces horizontally in equilibrium:
$$\Sigma F_x = T_B\cos 50^\circ - T_A\cos 40^\circ = 0$$
$$T_B = T_A\frac{\cos 40^\circ}{\cos 50^\circ} = T_A\tan 50^\circ \approx 1.1918 T_A$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Inspect the angles meeting at particle $O$:
- String $OA$ slopes upwards to the left at $40^\circ$ to the ceiling.
- String $OB$ slopes upwards to the right at $50^\circ$ to the ceiling.
Sum of inclination angles:
$$40^\circ + 50^\circ = 90^\circ \implies \angle AOB = 90^\circ$$

Equate horizontal components:
- Leftward pull: $T_A\cos 40^\circ$.
- Rightward pull: $T_B\cos 50^\circ$.
Balance them for equilibrium:
$$T_A\cos 40^\circ = T_B\cos 50^\circ \implies T_B = T_A\frac{\cos 40^\circ}{\cos 50^\circ}$$

ai_rubric.observable: States that the angles with the horizontal ceiling sum to $40^\circ + 50^\circ = 90^\circ$, so $\angle AOB = 180^\circ - 90^\circ = 90^\circ$.
Resolves horizontally in equilibrium: $T_A\cos 40^\circ = T_B\cos 50^\circ \implies T_B = T_A\frac{\cos 40^\circ}{\cos 50^\circ} = T_A\tan 50^\circ$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Core Practice 1: Two-string ceiling suspension with complementary inclinations

hints: Because strings $OA$ and $OB$ are perpendicular, the force triangle formed by $T_A$, $T_B$, and the vertical weight $W = 75\text{ N}$ is a right-angled triangle.
In this right-angled triangle of forces, $T_A = W\sin 40^\circ = 75\sin 40^\circ \approx 48.2\text{ N}$ and $T_B = W\sin 50^\circ = 75\sin 50^\circ \approx 57.5\text{ N}$.

walkthrough.text:
Use the closed right-angled force triangle formed by $T_A$, $T_B$, and weight $W = 75\text{ N}$:
Since $\angle AOB = 90^\circ$, the two tensions are perpendicular and weight $W$ acts as the hypotenuse:
$$T_A^2 + T_B^2 = W^2 = 75^2$$

Calculate tension $T_A$:
$$T_A = W\sin 40^\circ = 75\sin 40^\circ \approx 75(0.642788) = 48.209 \approx 48.2\text{ N}$$

Calculate tension $T_B$:
$$T_B = W\sin 50^\circ = 75\sin 50^\circ \approx 75(0.766044) = 57.453 \approx 57.5\text{ N}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Observe the power of the perpendicular triangle of forces:
- The downward weight $W = 75\text{ N}$ is the hypotenuse of the force triangle.
- Because $\angle AOB = 90^\circ$, each tension is simply a projection of the weight:
$$T_A = 75\sin 40^\circ, \quad T_B = 75\cos 40^\circ = 75\sin 50^\circ$$

Evaluate the tensions:
- Tension in string $OA$:
$$T_A = 75 \times 0.6428 \approx 48.2\text{ N}$$
- Tension in string $OB$:
$$T_B = 75 \times 0.7660 \approx 57.5\text{ N}$$

Verify with Pythagoras on the forces:
$$48.209^2 + 57.453^2 = 2324.1 + 3300.9 = 5625 = 75^2$$
This confirms the equilibrium solution.

ai_rubric.observable: Resolves vertically: $T_A\sin 40^\circ + T_B\sin 50^\circ = 75$ or resolves along string directions.

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured Practice: Core Practice 3: Asymmetrical two-string suspension with vertical angle references

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Core Practice 3: Asymmetrical two-string suspension with vertical angle references

hints: Remember that the angles are measured from the vertical, so horizontal components use sines and vertical components use cosines.
Resolve horizontally: the leftward horizontal component $T_A\sin 35^\circ$ balances the rightward component $T_B\sin 45^\circ$.
Resolve vertically: both upward components combine to support the weight: $T_A\cos 35^\circ + T_B\cos 45^\circ = 100$.

walkthrough.text:
Resolve forces horizontally in equilibrium:
$$\Sigma F_x = T_B\sin 45^\circ - T_A\sin 35^\circ = 0$$
$$T_A\sin 35^\circ = T_B\sin 45^\circ \implies T_B = T_A\frac{\sin 35^\circ}{\sin 45^\circ}$$

Resolve forces vertically in equilibrium:
$$\Sigma F_y = T_A\cos 35^\circ + T_B\cos 45^\circ - 100 = 0$$
$$T_A\cos 35^\circ + T_B\cos 45^\circ = 100$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Identify the geometry relative to the vertical line through the load:
- String $A$ is inclined at $35^\circ$ to the vertical.
- String $B$ is inclined at $45^\circ$ to the vertical.
Set horizontal balance:
$$T_A\sin 35^\circ = T_B\sin 45^\circ \implies T_B = T_A\frac{\sin 35^\circ}{\sin 45^\circ}$$

Set vertical balance:
- The upward vertical pulls support the $100\text{ N}$ load:
$$T_A\cos 35^\circ + T_B\cos 45^\circ = 100\text{ N}$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Core Practice 3: Asymmetrical two-string suspension with vertical angle references

hints: Substitute $T_B = T_A\frac{\sin 35^\circ}{\sin 45^\circ}$ into $T_A\cos 35^\circ + T_B\cos 45^\circ = 100$.
Factor out $T_A$: $T_A\left(\cos 35^\circ + \sin 35^\circ\frac{\cos 45^\circ}{\sin 45^\circ}\right) = T_A(\cos 35^\circ + \sin 35^\circ) = 100$.
Compute $T_A = \frac{100}{0.81915 + 0.57358} = \frac{100}{1.39273} \approx 71.8\text{ N}$, and find $T_B = 71.80\left(\frac{\sin 35^\circ}{\sin 45^\circ}\right) \approx 58.2\text{ N}$.

walkthrough.text:
Substitute $T_B = T_A\frac{\sin 35^\circ}{\sin 45^\circ}$ into the vertical equation:
$$T_A\cos 35^\circ + \left(T_A\frac{\sin 35^\circ}{\sin 45^\circ}\right)\cos 45^\circ = 100$$
Since $\frac{\cos 45^\circ}{\sin 45^\circ} = 1$:
$$T_A(\cos 35^\circ + \sin 35^\circ) = 100$$

Evaluate $T_A$ and $T_B$:
$$\cos 35^\circ + \sin 35^\circ \approx 0.819152 + 0.573576 = 1.392728$$
$$T_A = \frac{100}{1.392728} \approx 71.8015 \approx 71.8\text{ N}$$
$$T_B = 71.8015 \times \frac{\sin 35^\circ}{\sin 45^\circ} \approx 71.8015 \times \frac{0.573576}{0.707107} \approx 58.246 \approx 58.2\text{ N}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Notice the trigonometric simplification:
- Because $\tan 45^\circ = 1$, the vertical equation reduces elegantly:
$$T_A(\cos 35^\circ + \sin 35^\circ) = 100$$
$$T_A(1.3927) = 100 \implies T_A \approx 71.8\text{ N}$$

Calculate tension $T_B$:
$$T_B = 71.8 \times \frac{\sin 35^\circ}{\sin 45^\circ} \approx 58.2\text{ N}$$
String $A$ carries more load ($71.8\text{ N}$ compared to $58.2\text{ N}$) because it is steeper ($35^\circ$ to the vertical versus $45^\circ$).

ai_rubric.observable: Substitutes $T_B = T_A\frac{\sin 35^\circ}{\sin 45^\circ}$ into the vertical equation and isolates $T_A$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured Practice: Core Practice 4: Right-angled suspension triangle under horizontal load

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Core Practice 4: Right-angled suspension triangle under horizontal load

hints: Check the converse of Pythagoras theorem: $1.5^2 + 2.0^2 = 2.25 + 4.00 = 6.25 = 2.5^2$, which proves that $\triangle APB$ has a right angle at $P$.
In right-angled triangle $\triangle APB$, the angle $\alpha$ at vertex $A$ satisfies $\cos\alpha = \frac{AP}{AB} = \frac{1.5}{2.5} = 0.6$, and so $\sin\alpha = \sqrt{1 - 0.6^2} = 0.8$.
Similarly, the angle $\beta$ at vertex $B$ satisfies $\cos\beta = \frac{BP}{AB} = \frac{2.0}{2.5} = 0.8$ and $\sin\beta = 0.6$.

walkthrough.text:
Verify that $\triangle APB$ is right-angled using Pythagoras theorem:
$$AP^2 + BP^2 = 1.5^2 + 2.0^2 = 2.25 + 4.00 = 6.25 = 2.5^2 = AB^2$$
Because the squares sum to $AB^2$, the angle at $P$ is a right angle:
$$\angle APB = 90^\circ$$

Determine the direction ratios for string $AP$:
$$\cos\alpha = \frac{AP}{AB} = \frac{1.5}{2.5} = 0.6$$
$$\sin\alpha = \sqrt{1 - 0.6^2} = \sqrt{0.64} = 0.8$$

Determine the direction ratios for string $BP$:
$$\cos\beta = \frac{BP}{AB} = \frac{2.0}{2.5} = 0.8$$
$$\sin\beta = \sqrt{1 - 0.8^2} = \sqrt{0.36} = 0.6$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Identify the standard $3-4-5$ geometry:
- Lengths: $1.5\text{ m}$, $2.0\text{ m}$, and $2.5\text{ m}$.
- This is a $3-4-5$ right-angled triangle scaled by $0.5$:
$$1.5^2 + 2.0^2 = 2.5^2 \implies \angle APB = 90^\circ$$

Find the trigonometric ratios for string $AP$:
$$\cos\alpha = \frac{1.5}{2.5} = 0.6, \quad \sin\alpha = 0.8$$

Find the trigonometric ratios for string $BP$:
$$\cos\beta = \frac{2.0}{2.5} = 0.8, \quad \sin\beta = 0.6$$
Notice that $\alpha + \beta = 90^\circ$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Core Practice 4: Right-angled suspension triangle under horizontal load

hints: Calculate the weight $W = mg = 6(10) = 60\text{ N}$.
Resolve horizontally: $T_A\cos\alpha - T_B\cos\beta = F \implies 0.6 T_A - 0.8 T_B = 15$.
Resolve vertically: $T_A\sin\alpha + T_B\sin\beta = 60 \implies 0.8 T_A + 0.6 T_B = 60$. Multiply and add to find $T_A = 57\text{ N}$ and $T_B = 24\text{ N}$.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate the weight and set up horizontal equilibrium:
$$W = mg = 6(10) = 60\text{ N}$$
$$\Sigma F_x = F + T_B\cos\beta - T_A\cos\alpha = 0$$
$$0.6 T_A - 0.8 T_B = 15 \quad \text{--- (1)}$$

Set up vertical equilibrium:
$$\Sigma F_y = T_A\sin\alpha + T_B\sin\beta - 60 = 0$$
$$0.8 T_A + 0.6 T_B = 60 \quad \text{--- (2)}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Set up the simultaneous equations for the two string tensions:
- Horizontal balance (with horizontal pull $15\text{ N}$ to the right):
$$0.6 T_A - 0.8 T_B = 15$$
- Vertical balance (with downward weight $60\text{ N}$):
$$0.8 T_A + 0.6 T_B = 60$$

Eliminate $T_B$ by multiplying (1) by $0.6$ and (2) by $0.8$:
$$0.36 T_A - 0.48 T_B = 9$$
$$0.64 T_A + 0.48 T_B = 48$$
Adding both lines yields:
$$(0.36 + 0.64) T_A = 57 \implies T_A = 57\text{ N}$$

Find tension $T_B$:
$$0.6 T_B = 60 - 0.8(57) = 14.4 \implies T_B = 24\text{ N}$$
Both tensions are clean integers: $T_A = 57\text{ N}$ and $T_B = 24\text{ N}$.

ai_rubric.observable: Forms horizontal and vertical equilibrium equations: $0.6 T_A - 0.8 T_B = 15$ and $0.8 T_A + 0.6 T_B = 60$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured Practice: Core Practice 5: Smooth ring threaded on string across two ceiling supports

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Core Practice 5: Smooth ring threaded on string across two ceiling supports

hints: Because the ring is smooth, the tension $T$ is identical in both segments $AR$ and $BR$.
In the absence of horizontal forces, horizontal equilibrium gives $T\cos\theta_A = T\cos\theta_B \implies \cos\theta_A = \cos\theta_B$, so $\theta_A = \theta_B = \theta$.
By symmetry, the ring hangs centrally. Each segment has length $\frac{2.8}{2} = 1.4\text{ m}$ and half-span $\frac{2.0}{2} = 1.0\text{ m}$, so $\cos\theta = \frac{1.0}{1.4} = \frac{5}{7}$.

walkthrough.text:
Explain why the angles must be equal:
Because the ring is smooth, there is no friction and the tension $T$ is constant throughout both parts of the string. Horizontal equilibrium requires:
$$\Sigma F_x = T\cos\theta_B - T\cos\theta_A = 0 \implies \cos\theta_A = \cos\theta_B \implies \theta_A = \theta_B = \theta$$

Calculate the exact cosine using symmetry:
By symmetry, the ring sits at the midpoint between $A$ and $B$, dividing the total length of $2.8\text{ m}$ into two equal segments of $1.4\text{ m}$, with horizontal half-span $1.0\text{ m}$:
$$\cos\theta = \frac{\text{half-span}}{\text{segment length}} = \frac{1.0}{1.4} = \frac{5}{7}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Understand the behavior of a smooth ring:
- The ring slides until the forces balance.
- Equal tension on both sides ($T_{AR} = T_{BR} = T$) forces the horizontal pull to match:
